A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IPDreamer and have readable text, equations, figures, and references throughout. Neither contains an appendix. v2 refers to separate supplementary material that is absent from the supplied PDFs; its contents cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original qualitative 3D-generation results in Figures 1 and 3 and a comparison with four text-to-3D methods in Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 reports original generation and texture-editing outputs, a single-image-to-3D comparison, and component analyses in Figures 1 and 3–8.

M1.justification: The main NeRF-to-mesh pipeline and IPSD gradients remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds a task-specific adaptation: Zero123 guidance accompanies IPSD during texture optimization for single-image generation, whereas v1 describes Zero123 guidance only during NeRF training. The precise combination is deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates appearance-controlled text-to-3D generation. v2 additionally evaluates editing an existing Stage 1 reconstruction using different style images and single-image generation requiring strict reference-identity preservation (Sections 4.1 and 4.4). These substantially broaden the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: DreamFusion, Magic3D, Fantasia3D, and ProlificDreamer remain the text-to-3D comparators in v1 Figure 4 and v2 Figure 5. v2 Figure 6 adds comparisons against Zero123 and SyncDreamer for single-image generation.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs reuse a common Stage 1 NeRF across four style prompts per textual prompt, compare guidance methods using the same reference image, and examine geometry refinement and removal of the geometry prompt difference. v2 also uses DALL-E 3 references for four gallery prompts, expanding beyond v1's scribble/ControlNet example setup.

E4.justification: v1 contains no component ablations. v2 Section 4.5 adds normal-map comparisons before and after geometry optimization for two reference styles (Figure 7) and a sushi-car comparison with and without the geometry prompt difference (Figure 8). These provide new qualitative evidence about two central components.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The four editing samples per prompt in v2 represent different image prompts rather than documented repeated trials.

E6.justification: v2 adds texture-editing outcomes, a qualitative comparison favoring Zero123 plus IPSD, and findings from the component analyses. It also revises gallery examples and IPDreamer's cottage outputs in the retained text-to-3D comparison. These are added or replaced visual results; the PDFs establish no numerical or same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The SDS, VSD, Zero123-SDS, IPSD gradients, and geometry prompt difference definition are mathematically unchanged. v1's grouped geometry and texture gradients are separately numbered in v2, producing ten equation numbers instead of seven without adding mathematical substance.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit main contribution: modifying a 3D mesh's texture to match a supplied image style, with the claim that previous methods cannot achieve this. This extends the contribution beyond v1's controllable-generation claims, while the abstract and other central claims remain largely unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 introduces specific qualifications absent from v1: image guidance can override textual material descriptions, illustrated by a leather result under an 'iron breastplate' prompt, and IPSD alone cannot fully preserve reference-image identity. These clarify guidance priority and the boundary between style transfer and identity-preserving generation.

D1.justification: v2 identifies DALL-E 3 as the source of four gallery reference images and explains reuse of Stage 1 outputs for editing. It adds no concrete training budgets, optimizer settings, hardware specifications, or code-access information. Implementation details for combined Zero123/IPSD guidance are deferred to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: v2 adds SyncDreamer and removes citations to Controllable Mind Visual Diffusion Model and Face Animation with an Attribute-Guided Diffusion Model. It also positions image-prompt style editing as unavailable in previous methods. Most related-work discussion is retained; the additional Takagi–Nishimoto entry duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall section order remain intact. The experiments receive more descriptive subsections and additional explanations, with limited introductory rewriting. The conclusion also corrects its reversed assignment of RGB images and normal maps to texture and geometry optimization.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column teaser with a full-width editing/generation figure, rebuilds the generation gallery with explicit mesh views, and adds dedicated editing, single-image comparison, and component-analysis figures. Existing examples are also redistributed, including the dragon examples moving into Figure 1. This substantially changes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 relies on showcases and one qualitative baseline comparison. v2 improves support for appearance control through shared-initialization editing examples and targeted component comparisons, while explicitly acknowledging an identity-preservation limitation. The gains remain limited by selected qualitative examples and missing hybrid-guidance implementation details; the stronger claim that previous methods cannot perform the editing is not supported by a direct editing-baseline comparison.
